finding: Chronic effects depended on sex and β4 genotype.

finding: Functional and binding data plus proposed pore and non-pore locations.

finding: Parent and hydroxy metabolite both inhibit currents.
limitation: Hydroxy stereochemistry not individually resolved; another receptor family, not α7.

finding: Approximately twofold state-dependent difference in affinity.
limitation: α7 assays in this paper concern coronaridine compounds; do not attribute those results to bupropion.

title: Molecular basis of atypicality of bupropion inferred from its receptor engagement in nervous system tissues.
finding: Proposes tissue-specific contributions of multiple targets.
limitation: Secondary use of affinity data, not a new receptor potency experiment.

title: Blockade of nicotinic acetylcholine receptor enhances the responsiveness to bupropion in the mouse forced swim test.
finding: Subunit deletions and DHβE altered behavioral responses.
limitation: Not a test of α7 blockade or depersonalization.

title: Bupropion Inhibits Serotonin Type 3AB Heteromeric Channels at Clinically Relevant Concentrations.
finding: Coapplication IC50 840 and 526 µM, respectively; preincubation increases inhibition.
limitation: Do not substitute preincubation effects for coapplication IC50 or infer human exposure from the title.

title: Different Classes of Antidepressants Inhibit the Rat α7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor by Interacting within the Ion Channel: A Functional and Structural Study.
finding: Current ratio 0.52 ± 0.04 at 50 µM; inhibition also observed at 20 µM.
limitation: Single-concentration current ratio is not a newly fitted IC50. Pore location also uses a homology-model workflow.

title: Disruption of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory response by R5-tropic HIV-1 protein gp120JRFL.
preparation: human monocyte-derived macrophages exposed to HIV gp120
finding: 70 ng/mL bupropion reduced IL-6 in the tested paradigm, not all cytokines.
limitation: Downstream inflammatory response; does not establish selective α7 channel inhibition at that concentration.

title: Type I and type II positive allosteric modulators of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors induce antidepressant-like activity in mice by a mechanism involving receptor potentiation but not neurotransmitter reuptake inhibition. Correlation with mTOR intracellular pathway activation.
finding: PAM-2 and bupropion showed behavioral synergy.
limitation: Not a bupropion α7 concentration-response assay or evidence that α7 antagonism explains antidepressant efficacy.

title: An integrated approach for early in vitro seizure prediction utilizing hiPSC neurons and human ion channel assays.
receptor: human 14-channel panel including α4β2; no α7
preparation: engineered human channels; separate hiPSC neuronal cultures
finding: Reported channel hits were potassium channels and α4β2; bupropion also changed neuronal network bursting.
source_verification: primary PDF methods and results text
source_location: Table 1; Results: CNS active therapies; hiPSC neuronal coculture assay
limitation: Panel does not assay α7. Network effects do not identify the causal channel or prove the mechanism of clinical seizures; individual Figure 1 potencies not extracted.

title: A bupropion modulatory site in the Gloeobacter violaceus ligand-gated ion channel.
finding: Wild-type IC50 about 15 µM; T214F increased it about 13-fold; supports an intersubunit modulatory site.
limitation: Bacterial homolog, not human α7. 2023 preprint and 2024 article are one study, not two replications.

title: Effects of hydroxymetabolites of bupropion on nicotine dependence behavior in mice.
method: conditioned place preference; withdrawal; drug discrimination
finding: S,S metabolite was more potent in several nicotine-dependence endpoints; R,R differed across tasks.
source_verification: primary indexed full-text results and discussion
limitation: Behavior and reference receptor values are not a new α7 potency measurement; higher doses produced reward themselves.

title: Comparison of the behavioral effects of bupropion and psychostimulants.
finding: No PPI disruption was found under the tested conditions, unlike psychostimulant comparators.
limitation: Challenges an automatic bupropion-to-gating-deficit prediction; mouse PPI is not human P50 or depersonalization.

title: Convulsive liability of bupropion hydrochloride metabolites in Swiss albino mice.
compound: bupropion; hydroxy-, threo- and erythrohydrobupropion HCl
preparation: female Swiss albino mice; 10 per dose group
method: single intraperitoneal equimolar dosing; 2 h observation
finding: Metabolites produced more convulsions than parent at the upper tested doses.
limitation: No individual enantiomer resolution or α7 mechanism. Doses were bupropion-HCl equivalents, not equal metabolite mass. Parent CD50 is extrapolated beyond tested range; discussion inconsistently says parent was not evaluated.

title: Convulsant and anticonvulsant effects of bupropion in mice.
method: maximal electroshock, PTZ, kainate; bupropion dose-response
finding: Lower doses protected against electroshock; higher doses were convulsant; no effect on PTZ/kainate outcomes.
limitation: Dose/model dependence does not establish α7 mediation or justify therapeutic use against human seizures.

title: Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor α7 Subunit Is an Essential Regulator of Seizure Susceptibility.
preparation: wild-type male mice; pilocarpine challenge; slices
finding: α7 blockade shortened seizure latencies and increased pyramidal firing; agonist did not significantly improve these outcomes.
limitation: No bupropion. PV interpretation uses staining/pharmacology, not PV-specific genetic receptor deletion.

title: Nicotine Elicits Convulsive Seizures by Activating Amygdalar Neurons.
method: nicotine seizures; antagonist pretreatment; Fos; lesions and microinjection
finding: MLA reduced nicotine-induced seizures; amygdala manipulations supported a role in this model.
source_verification: primary indexed full-text methods and results
limitation: MLA 10 mg/kg systemic pretreatment is pharmacological attribution, not cell-specific genetic proof; not a bupropion experiment.

title: Absence of alpha7-containing neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors does not prevent nicotine-induced seizures.
finding: Seizure dose-response curves were similar across genotypes.
limitation: Null result concerns this nicotine challenge; it does not establish no α7 role in every circuit or seizure model. Lifelong deletion differs from acute blockade.

title: Genetic and pharmacological strategies identify a behavioral function of neuronal nicotinic receptors.
finding: MLA and DHβE did not block nicotine seizures and themselves caused seizures in this paradigm.
limitation: Route and dose context differ from systemic antagonist studies; pharmacological labels alone do not demonstrate exclusive subtype mediation.

title: α7 nicotinic receptors contributes to glutamatergic activity in the hippocampus of patients with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (MTLE-HS).
preparation: resected hippocampal tissue from patients with MTLE-HS
finding: Antagonist altered frequency and amplitude of glutamatergic events.
limitation: Full text unavailable; direction and size not resolved from abstract. Diseased human tissue, not bupropion exposure or depersonalization.

title: Inhibition and disinhibition of pyramidal neurons by activation of nicotinic receptors on hippocampal interneurons.
finding: Nicotinic excitation of interneurons produced either inhibition or disinhibition of pyramidal neurons.
limitation: Some currents were non-α7; net circuit sign depends on connections. No bupropion or human symptom measurement.

title: alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on GABAergic interneurons evoke dendritic and somatic inhibition of hippocampal neurons.
finding: MLA-sensitive somatic/dendritic inhibition of pyramidal cells and inhibition between interneurons.
limitation: No direct pyramidal disinhibition observed in tested pairs; interneuron-to-interneuron inhibition suggests that possibility. No bupropion.

title: Cholinergic axons modulate GABAergic signaling among hippocampal interneurons via postsynaptic alpha 7 nicotinic receptors.
receptor: postsynaptic α7 modulation of GABAA responses
finding: α7 activation depressed GABAergic currents onto interneurons, with a small presynaptic release increase.
limitation: Postsynaptic currents onto inhibitory cells must not be equated to GABA output onto pyramidal neurons. No bupropion.

title: Proof-of-concept trial of an alpha7 nicotinic agonist in schizophrenia.
finding: P50 inhibition improved during agonist treatment.
limitation: Small agonist trial in schizophrenia, not antagonist/metabolite study or depersonalization; does not imply symmetric effects of blockade.

title: Allosteric alpha-7 nicotinic receptor modulation and P50 sensory gating in schizophrenia: a proof-of-mechanism study.
finding: No improvement in P50 or other tested electrophysiological markers.
limitation: Different compound and population from agonist studies; limits generalization without disproving all α7 effects.

title: Alpha4beta2 nicotinic receptor stimulation contributes to the effects of nicotine in the DBA/2 mouse model of sensory gating.
receptor: α4β2 and other nicotinic sensory-gating pathways
finding: α4β2 blockade removed nicotine enhancement of the first response; gating-ratio improvement partly persisted.
limitation: Gating ratio is influenced by both responses; α7 is not the only nicotinic contributor.

title: Dissociative identity disorder and prepulse inhibition of the acoustic startle reflex.
finding: Depersonalization subgroup broadly resembled controls; prolonged PPI and absent habituation concerned DID.
source_verification: primary indexed full-text methods and results
limitation: Only 2 had depersonalization alone, 6 also amnesia; small heterogeneous, medication-unmatched groups. Not P50 or α7 assay.

title: Detached and distracted: ERP correlates of altered attentional function in depersonalisation.
finding: Reduced suppression of unattended stimuli in the P1 interval, 135–150 ms.
source_verification: primary abstract and institutional repository abstract
limitation: Visual P1 is not auditory P50 or PPI; no α7 intervention or bupropion exposure.

title: Associations of P50 suppression and desensitization with perceptual and cognitive features of "unreality" in schizotypy.
finding: Poorer P50 suppression correlated with perceptual anomalies and magical ideation.
limitation: Unreality here is a schizotypy construct, not diagnosed DPDR; correlation does not identify α7 or causation.

title: Effects of analgesics and antidepressants on TREK-2 and TRESK currents.
finding: Inhibited TRESK; no effect on TREK-2 under tested conditions.
limitation: Different channel species; no metabolite or alpha7 experiment, human target engagement, or seizure mediation demonstrated. Abstract and figure caption report different replicate counts; no pooled n inferred.

title: α7-nAChR agonist enhances neural plasticity in the hippocampus via a GABAergic circuit.
preparation: rat septo-hippocampal slices and CA1 pyramidal neurons
finding: Agonist increased GABA IPSC frequency and reduced evoked firing; 50 nM MLA increased evoked firing and blocked the agonist effect.
source_verification: primary full-text methods, results and figures
limitation: Supports a circuit link under these conditions; no bupropion, metabolite, depersonalization or seizure endpoint. Pharmacological attribution is not cell-specific genetic proof.

title: Development of a Rat Plasma and Brain Extracellular Fluid Pharmacokinetic Model for Bupropion and Hydroxybupropion Based on Microdialysis Sampling, and Application to Predict Human Brain Concentrations.
preparation: rats; quantitative plasma and brain extracellular microdialysis
method: measured unbound concentrations with fitted compartmental model
finding: Rat steady-state brain ECF/unbound-plasma ratio estimates 1.9 and 1.7; human exposure was predicted by translation.
limitation: Fitted ratios and translated human predictions are not measured human free-brain concentrations or alpha7 engagement; not stereoisomer-resolved in this record.
evidence_layer: published brain distribution evidence; no new exposure modeling

title: Characterization of the Stereoselective Disposition of Bupropion and Its Metabolites in Rat Plasma and Brain.
compound: bupropion; hydroxy-, threo- and erythro metabolites
stereochemistry: parent enantiomers and metabolite stereoisomers resolved
preparation: rats given racemic parent or preformed S,S hydroxy metabolite
method: stereoselective LC-MS/MS plus companion equilibrium dialysis
finding: Unbound brain/plasma ratios varied over time; at 4–6 h were below 1 for parent enantiomers and approximately 1 for formed metabolites.
limitation: Rat exposure experiment using a different method from microdialysis; no measured human alpha7 engagement. Whole-brain total concentrations cannot be substituted for unbound concentrations.
evidence_layer: published brain distribution evidence; no new exposure modeling

title: Depersonalization- and derealization-like phenomena of epileptic origin.
preparation: 9 ictal DP; 7 ictal DR; 28 experiential-symptom epilepsy controls
finding: Ictal DP was predominantly associated with frontal epilepsy; DR with temporal epilepsy.
limitation: Selected drug-resistant epilepsy population; simultaneous DP/DR excluded. No bupropion or alpha7 measurement; does not establish that primary DPDR is epilepsy or a dose continuum.

title: SSRI versus bupropion effects on symptom clusters in suicidal depression: post hoc analysis of a randomized clinical trial.
preparation: 74 depressed adults with current suicidal thoughts or past attempt
method: post hoc analysis of randomized double-blind 8-week trial
finding: No differential treatment effect on the Disturbed Thinking factor, which includes a DP/DR item.
source_verification: primary indexed full-text results and figure footnote
limitation: Composite also includes insight, paranoia and obsessions/compulsions. Not a separate DPDR efficacy/adverse-event analysis; null composite does not exclude individual DP/DR effects or test alpha7.

title: Association Study of CHRNA7 Promoter Variants with Sensory and Sensorimotor Gating in Schizophrenia Patients and Healthy Controls: A Danish Case-Control Study.
finding: Variant associated with schizophrenia but not P50 suppression or PPI; variants associated with startle magnitude.
limitation: Genetic association and sensory registration are not proof of alpha7-dependent gating or bupropion effects.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: P50 amplitude reduction: a nicotinic receptor-mediated deficit in first-degree relatives of schizophrenia patients.
finding: Relatives showed reduced initial P50 amplitude with normal gating; nicotine effects depended on smoking/withdrawal state.
limitation: Initial-response amplitude differs from gating; nicotine is not alpha7 selective.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Nicotinic modulation of auditory evoked potential electroencephalography in a rodent neurodevelopmental model of schizophrenia.
finding: Strong trend for N40 improvement; significant mismatch-negativity improvement with ABT-107.
limitation: Trend is not a significant gating rescue; no bupropion or depersonalization.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Combining CDP-choline and galantamine, an optimized α7 nicotinic strategy, to ameliorate sensory gating to speech stimuli in schizophrenia.
finding: Combination improved speech P50 measures in low suppressors.
limitation: Subgroup and mixed cholinergic intervention; not isolated alpha7 causality.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of tropisetron in patients with schizophrenia.
finding: P50 improvement reported in nonsmoking subgroup.
limitation: Tropisetron has 5-HT3 activity; subgroup clinical finding is not a bupropion or DPDR experiment.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Neuronal nicotinic receptors in synaptic functions in humans and rats: physiological and clinical relevance.

finding: Interneuron nicotinic activation triggers GABA release; circuit effects can inhibit or disinhibit pyramidal neurons.
limitation: Receptor subtype and target-cell connections determine sign; no metabolite pharmacology.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Involvement of nicotinic and muscarinic receptors in the endogenous cholinergic modulation of the balance between excitation and inhibition in the young rat visual cortex.
finding: Endogenous ACh enhanced inhibitory dominance; alpha4beta2 blockade depressed inhibition.
limitation: Supports cholinergic control but cannot be cited as a specifically alpha7/PV result.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Reduced GABAergic inhibition in the basolateral amygdala and the development of anxiety-like behaviors after mild traumatic brain injury.
finding: After injury inhibition declined but alpha7-mediated currents and surface expression increased.

evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Emotional Experience and Awareness of Self: Functional MRI Studies of Depersonalization Disorder.
method: fMRI and skin conductance; uncontrolled treatment follow-up
finding: Reduced insula response associated with emotional numbing; improvement associated with increased insula activity.
source_verification: primary abstract and Scite full-text methods

title: Altered Self-Referential-Related Brain Regions in Depersonalization-Derealization Disorder.
finding: Altered insula/cortical-midline connectivity correlated with symptom dimensions.
limitation: Cross-sectional association, not receptor mechanism; classification accuracy not a validated causal biomarker.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: How do you feel when you can't feel your body? Interoception, functional connectivity and emotional processing in depersonalization-derealization disorder.
finding: Patient showed impaired heartbeat task performance and reduced connectivity in interoceptive state.
limitation: Single-case evidence cannot establish a universal DPDR mechanism.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Huperzine A attenuates epileptic seizures via enhancing dCA1-projecting septal cholinergic transmission.
method: cholinergic-cell ablation, fiber photometry and regional pharmacology
finding: Hup A reduced seizures; septal cholinergic ablation and alpha7 pharmacological interference reversed protection.
limitation: Ablated cells were cholinergic; this is not alpha7 deletion specifically in PV or SST cells. No bupropion.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: α7-Containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on interneurons of the basolateral amygdala and their role in the regulation of the network excitability.
finding: Basal alpha7 activity supports inhibition; agonism increased inhibition more than excitation under tested conditions.
limitation: Circuit-specific net effect; does not establish drug-induced symptoms.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Reduced Chrna7 expression in mice is associated with decreases in hippocampal markers of inhibitory function: implications for neuropsychiatric diseases.
finding: Reduced GAD65 and sex-dependent GABAA-receptor changes; GABA content unchanged.
limitation: Developmental gene dosage differs from acute antagonism; no bupropion or clinical dissociation.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Increased sensitivity to nicotine-induced seizures in mice heterozygous for the L250T mutation in the alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor.
finding: Mutants had greater nicotine seizure sensitivity; MLA inhibited induced seizures.
limitation: Shows activation can be proconvulsant in a different condition; not a wild-type bupropion experiment.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Chrna7 deficient mice manifest no consistent neuropsychiatric and behavioral phenotypes.
method: 12 behavioral assessments and freely moving EEG
finding: No consistent behavioral/EEG phenotype detected with decreased Chrna7 copy number.
source_verification: primary abstract and retrieved full text
limitation: Retain null results; strain and developmental compensation limit transfer to acute drug blockade.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Mecamylamine inhibits seizure-like activity in CA1-CA3 hippocampus through antagonism to nicotinic receptors.
finding: Mecamylamine blocked discharges; alpha7 and alpha4beta2 antagonists did not.
limitation: Pharmacological isolation and seizure-like slice activity differ from intact-brain drug seizures.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Exploring the ameliorative role of α7 neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptor modulation in epilepsy and associated comorbidities in post-PTZ-kindled mice.
finding: Choline ameliorated severity and comorbid behaviors; MLA did not ameliorate them.
limitation: An absence of improvement is not demonstrated worsening; ligands and metabolic actions need specificity controls.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Cytisine Exerts an Anti-Epileptic Effect via α7nAChRs in a Rat Model of Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
method: three-week treatment and video seizure monitoring
finding: Cytisine reduced seizures; antagonist opposed effects; glutamate declined while bulk GABA did not change.
limitation: Mixed-target drug; bulk transmitter content does not measure inhibitory synaptic flux. Related research program to tropisetron study.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Tropisetron, an Antiemetic Drug, Exerts an Anti-Epileptic Effect Through the Activation of α7nAChRs in a Rat Model of Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
method: three-week treatment and video seizure monitoring
finding: Tropisetron reduced recurrent seizures and glutamate; measured GABA content unchanged.
limitation: Pharmacological attribution with mixed-target ligand; not direct proof of an alpha7-GABA-bupropion chain.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Direct Septum-Hippocampus Cholinergic Circuit Attenuates Seizure Through Driving Somatostatin Inhibition.
compound: septal cholinergic and hippocampal cell manipulations
preparation: 42 TLE patients/22 controls for imaging; separate mouse models
finding: Cholinergic activation reduced mouse seizures; silencing SST, but not PV, cells reversed protection.
limitation: Human imaging is observational; mouse causal cell-type result does not establish alpha7 as sole receptor or transfer to bupropion.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Region-independent active CNS net uptake of marketed H+/OC antiporter system substrates.
method: regional concentration/binding and brain-slice uptake measurements
finding: Estimated whole-brain unbound/plasma ratio 1.94 ± 0.57; active uptake and intracellular trapping were distinguished.
source_verification: primary indexed full-text results and Table 3
limitation: Rat parent drug; not metabolite-specific human alpha7 engagement. No new exposure calculation made.
evidence_layer: published brain distribution evidence; no new exposure modeling

title: Inhibition of G protein-activated inwardly rectifying K+ channels by various antidepressant drugs.
finding: Bupropion was an exception to inhibition observed with several other antidepressants.
limitation: Retain negative target evidence; other potassium-channel findings do not imply all K channels are inhibited.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Effects of acute treatment with antidepressant drugs on sensorimotor gating deficits in rats.
finding: Bupropion did not reverse either tested PPI deficit.
limitation: Failure to rescue induced deficits is not evidence that bupropion causes a deficit.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Bupropion-induced convulsions: preclinical evaluation of antiepileptic drugs.
finding: Some drugs protected against bupropion-induced convulsions; others failed despite motor impairment.
limitation: Seizure suppression by GABA-related treatment cannot identify the initiating bupropion target; not clinical efficacy guidance.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence

title: Selective deuteration of bupropion slows epimerization and reduces metabolism.
finding: Deuteration reduced metabolite formation and slowed racemization.
limitation: Analogues are not human metabolites; proposed reduced toxicity was not established by the metabolism measurements.
evidence_layer: circuit, seizure, sensory or competing-mechanism evidence
